lessons.title: Why is Lemon Juice Sour? Acids Release H⁺ Ions in Water (Arrhenius Definition)

quiz.prompt: Pure water has pH 7.0 and H⁺ concentration of 1 x 10⁻⁷ mol/L. Which statement about the H⁺ ions in pure water is correct?
choices: It has a tiny amount of H⁺, far less than lemon juice
It has more H⁺ than vinegar
It has the same amount of H⁺ as lemon juice
It has no H⁺ ions at all
quiz.rationale: 1 x 10⁻⁷ mol/L is very small but not zero, and it is much less than lemon juice (1 x 10⁻² mol/L) or vinegar (about 1.6 x 10⁻³ mol/L).
quiz.placement: Part A (data): data card with pH and H+ concentration

quiz.prompt: Lemon juice has pH 2.0 and H⁺ = 1 x 10⁻² mol/L. Vinegar has pH 2.8 and H⁺ about 1.6 x 10⁻³ mol/L. About how many times more H⁺ does lemon juice have than vinegar?
choices: About 0.8 times
About 10 times
About 6 times
About 60 times
quiz.rationale: Divide the concentrations: (1 x 10⁻²) ÷ (1.6 x 10⁻³) = 6.25, which is about 6 times. The pH difference of 0.8 does not mean 0.8 times more H⁺, because each pH unit is a 10-fold change.
quiz.placement: Part A (data): 'How many times more H+ does lemon juice have than vinegar?'

quiz.prompt: In a particle simulation, acid molecules from lemon juice dissolve in water. What do learners see happen?
choices: The acid molecules stay whole and release nothing
The acid molecules turn into sugar particles
The acid molecules remove all the water particles
The acid molecules release H⁺ (aq) ions into the water
quiz.rationale: An acid dissolving in water releases H⁺ (aq) ions. This is the particle-level change that explains the properties of acids.
quiz.placement: Part B (simulation or paper model): acid molecules dissolving in water and releasing H+ (aq) ions

quiz.prompt: Which statement is the Arrhenius definition of an acid?
choices: A substance that is harmful if swallowed
A substance that contains no water
A substance that produces H⁺ (aq) ions when dissolved in water
A substance that tastes sour in the laboratory
quiz.rationale: The Arrhenius definition says an acid produces H⁺ (aq) ions in water. Being harmful or tasting sour is not the definition, and we never taste chemicals in the laboratory.
quiz.placement: Pairs' CER explanation and the class definition recorded on the board

quiz.prompt: Lemon juice (pH 2.0) and vinegar (pH 2.8) are both acids. Why does lemon juice have the lower pH?
choices: It contains no water, but vinegar does
It has fewer H⁺ ions than vinegar
It has a higher concentration of H⁺ ions than vinegar
It contains more sugar than vinegar
quiz.rationale: A lower pH means a higher H⁺ concentration. Lemon juice has about 6 times more H⁺ (1 x 10⁻² mol/L) than vinegar (about 1.6 x 10⁻³ mol/L).
quiz.placement: Claim-evidence-reasoning: 'Why is lemon juice sour, and why does it have a lower pH than vinegar?'

quiz.prompt: Stomach acid is hydrochloric acid. Which particle does it release when it dissolves in water, making it an acid?
choices: No particles, because it is a liquid
Only water particles
H⁺ (aq) ions
Sugar particles
quiz.rationale: Hydrochloric acid is an acid, so by the Arrhenius definition it releases H⁺ (aq) ions in water, just like the acids in lemon juice and vinegar.
quiz.placement: Driving Question Board: linking notes to the hyperacidity question

quiz.prompt: In a Model drawing, lemon juice (H⁺ = 1 x 10⁻² mol/L) is shown with 6 H⁺ dots. Which drawing for vinegar (about 1.6 x 10⁻³ mol/L) and water (1 x 10⁻⁷ mol/L) is best?
choices: Vinegar 6 dots, water 0 dots
Vinegar 1 dot, water almost no dots
Vinegar 1 dot, water exactly 0 dots
Vinegar 12 dots, water 6 dots
quiz.rationale: Lemon juice has about 6 times more H⁺ than vinegar, so 6 dots against 1 dot. Water has a tiny amount of H⁺, so it is drawn with almost none, not exactly zero.
quiz.placement: Model page: three boxes for lemon juice, vinegar and water showing H+ (aq) ions

quiz.prompt: Lemon juice turns blue litmus paper red. Which explanation uses the idea from this lesson?
choices: Lemon juice contains H⁺ (aq) ions released by its acid in water
Lemon juice is red in colour
Lemon juice has no water particles
Lemon juice contains sugar particles
quiz.rationale: Acids release H⁺ (aq) ions in water. These ions explain the low pH, the sour taste and the colour change of indicators such as litmus.
quiz.placement: End of lesson: linking H+ ions to the litmus and indicator colours from Lessons 2-3
